questions.stem: A 6-week-old infant is evaluated twice for poor feeding and tachypnea. At the second visit, heart rate is 184/min despite being afebrile and calm. There is mild hepatomegaly and a gallop. Which feature should most strongly prompt evaluation for myocarditis rather than attributing the tachycardia to a viral illness?

options.A: Persistent tachycardia out of proportion to fever or agitation

questions.rationale: Persistent disproportionate tachycardia is a classic warning sign, especially when paired with gallop and hepatomegaly.

option_explanations.A: Correct. It should trigger reconsideration of a purely respiratory or febrile diagnosis.
option_explanations.B: Young age increases vulnerability but is not specific.
option_explanations.C: Nasal congestion is common and nonspecific.
option_explanations.E: Normal oxygen saturation does not exclude cardiac failure.

questions.board_pearl: An afebrile infant with persistent marked tachycardia deserves a cardiac explanation until proven otherwise.

questions.stem: An 11-year-old has chest pain, fever, elevated troponin, and mild LV dysfunction. Blood cultures grow Staphylococcus aureus and echocardiography shows a new valvar vegetation. Which diagnosis should take priority over presumed isolated viral myocarditis?

options.A: Infective endocarditis with myocardial involvement or secondary dysfunction

questions.rationale: A bloodstream pathogen plus vegetation establishes a different primary infectious cardiac diagnosis that can produce myocardial dysfunction.

option_explanations.A: Correct. The microbiologic and echocardiographic findings define the key process.
option_explanations.B: Does not explain bacteremia or cardiac findings.
option_explanations.C: Does not explain troponin or vegetation.
option_explanations.D: Does not explain vegetation and bacteremia.

questions.board_pearl: Do not let an elevated troponin force all cardiac inflammation into the myocarditis label.

questions.stem: A 14-year-old with suspected myocarditis has chest pain and palpitations. Which test is most useful for detecting intermittent arrhythmias during the acute hospitalization?
questions.rationale: Continuous telemetry provides ongoing rhythm surveillance and can detect episodic atrial, ventricular, or conduction abnormalities.

option_explanations.A: Correct. Intermittent electrical instability may be missed on a single ECG.
option_explanations.C: Electrolytes may identify contributors but do not detect the arrhythmia itself.

questions.board_pearl: A normal snapshot ECG does not substitute for rhythm monitoring in a patient at ongoing electrical risk.

questions.stem: A 2-year-old with suspected myocarditis has pulmonary edema, hepatomegaly, and poor perfusion. A clinician proposes another 20 mL/kg rapid fluid bolus because the child is tachycardic. What is the best response?

options.A: Give the bolus because tachycardia proves hypovolemia
options.B: Reassess volume status and cardiac output before additional fluid because excess preload may worsen congestion
options.E: Ignore the perfusion findings until troponin returns

questions.rationale: Tachycardia is not synonymous with hypovolemia. In myocardial dysfunction with pulmonary/systemic congestion, additional rapid fluid can worsen heart failure.

option_explanations.B: Correct. Fluid decisions must follow the hemodynamic phenotype.
option_explanations.D: Oral fluid does not solve cardiogenic shock and may still worsen congestion.
option_explanations.E: Treatment should not wait for biomarkers.

questions.board_pearl: Before giving fluid in shock, ask whether the problem is preload depletion or pump failure.

questions.stem: A 12-year-old with suspected myocarditis has an echocardiogram showing a small pericardial effusion, mild LV dilation, and depressed systolic function. Which statement is most accurate?

options.A: These findings are compatible with myocarditis but are not individually specific
options.B: A pericardial effusion excludes myocardial disease
options.D: The echo determines the viral pathogen
options.E: A normal coronary origin means myocarditis is impossible

questions.rationale: Echo abnormalities in myocarditis are variable and supportive rather than pathognomonic.

option_explanations.A: Correct. Echo should be integrated with the clinical picture and other testing.
option_explanations.B: Pericardial and myocardial inflammation can coexist.
option_explanations.C: LV dysfunction has many acquired and congenital causes.
option_explanations.E: Normal coronary origins help exclude a mimic but do not exclude myocarditis.

questions.board_pearl: Echo is essential for function and anatomy, not for proving etiology.

questions.stem: A 16-year-old endurance athlete has sinus bradycardia at baseline and mild LV enlargement but no symptoms, normal troponin, normal systolic function, and no recent illness. Which diagnosis is more likely than myocarditis?
questions.rationale: Asymptomatic athletic remodeling with preserved function and no inflammatory evidence is more likely than acute myocarditis.

option_explanations.A: Correct. The phenotype is chronic, physiologic, and noninflammatory.
option_explanations.B: Fulminant myocarditis causes severe acute illness.
option_explanations.D: No chest pain or pericarditic findings are present.
option_explanations.E: ALCAPA presents in infancy and would not fit this benign athletic phenotype.

questions.board_pearl: Context matters: chamber size alone is not myocardial inflammation.

questions.stem: An 8-year-old with myocarditis develops worsening respiratory distress and pulmonary edema with declining mental status. Which principle is most appropriate regarding respiratory support?

options.A: Escalate oxygenation/ventilatory support as needed while recognizing the hemodynamic consequences of positive pressure
options.B: Avoid all respiratory support because it masks tachypnea
options.D: Wait for CMR before treating hypoxemia

questions.rationale: Respiratory failure should be treated promptly, but ventilation in cardiogenic shock requires careful hemodynamic management because induction and positive pressure can affect preload and afterload.

option_explanations.A: Correct. Airway/ventilation and circulation must be managed together.
option_explanations.E: Sedation without adequate airway/hemodynamic planning can worsen instability.

questions.board_pearl: In severe myocarditis, airway decisions are cardiovascular decisions too.

questions.stem: Which acute feature in a child with myocarditis should increase concern for a complicated hospital course?

options.C: Normal blood pressure with no symptoms

questions.rationale: Clinically significant arrhythmias in pediatric myocarditis are associated with greater morbidity and mortality and indicate electrical instability.

option_explanations.A: Correct. Tachyarrhythmia is a meaningful adverse-risk marker.

questions.board_pearl: The presence of arrhythmia changes risk stratification even before severe pump failure develops.

questions.stem: A 5-year-old with a systemic autoimmune disorder develops chest pain, elevated troponin, and LV dysfunction. What is the most appropriate etiologic approach?

options.A: Consider myocarditis as a manifestation of the underlying inflammatory disease
options.B: Assume all childhood myocarditis is viral
options.C: Exclude myocarditis because the child has a known diagnosis
options.E: Diagnose congenital heart disease without imaging

questions.rationale: Myocarditis can be immune-mediated and may occur as part of systemic inflammatory disease.

option_explanations.A: Correct. Etiology should be linked to the clinical context.
option_explanations.B: Viral causes are common but not exclusive.
option_explanations.C: A known autoimmune disease can increase rather than eliminate suspicion.
option_explanations.D: The history may directly inform cause and treatment.

questions.board_pearl: Always ask whether myocarditis is primary or part of a systemic inflammatory process.

questions.stem: A 15-year-old with prior myocarditis has persistent late gadolinium enhancement on follow-up CMR despite normalized LV function. Which statement is most appropriate?

options.A: Residual myocardial scar may have prognostic and arrhythmic relevance and should be interpreted by cardiology
options.B: Persistent LGE proves active bacterial infection
options.C: LGE is always benign once EF normalizes
options.D: No rhythm surveillance is ever needed
options.E: The finding is unrelated to prior myocarditis

questions.rationale: LGE can reflect residual myocardial injury/scar and may remain relevant to risk assessment even after functional recovery.

option_explanations.A: Correct. Tissue recovery and functional recovery are not identical.
option_explanations.B: LGE is not specific for bacterial infection.
option_explanations.C: Persistent scar should not automatically be dismissed.
option_explanations.D: Rhythm assessment may be important depending on the clinical context.
option_explanations.E: It can be a residual marker of the prior inflammatory injury.

questions.board_pearl: Follow-up after myocarditis should consider function, symptoms, rhythm, and tissue injury—not EF alone.
